podcast.title: Death from Bile Duct Cancer (Summer 2014)
podcast.body: Tommy Ramone, the drummer for the Ramones, passed away from bile duct cancer in the summer of 2014, marking the death of the last original member of the iconic punk band. "and drummer Tommy Ramon was taken by Bile Duck Cancer in the summer of 2014."

podcast.title: Founding Member of The Ramones
podcast.body: Tommy was one of the four members who formed The Ramones a year after Douglas Colvin (D.D.) and John Cummings (Johnny) purchased their initial instruments at Manie's Music in 1973. "A year later, Douglas was calling himself D.D. and Johnny was Johnny. And together with Joey and Tommy, they formed the Ramones."

xref.title: Deaths of Original Members (2001-2014)
xref.body: The original lineup of the Ramones tragically passed away over a 13-year period: Joey Ramone in 2001, Dee Dee Ramone in 2002, Johnny Ramone in 2004, and Tommy Ramone in 2014, marking the end of an era for the seminal punk band. "He was the first of the original Ramones to die. Base player DD Ramon died of a heroin overdose the following summer. Whereas Johnny Ramon lost his fight with prostate cancer in September 2004, and drummer Tommy Ramon was taken by Bile Duck Cancer in the summer of 2014."

xref.title: Last Original Member Alive (2002/2005)
xref.body: As of 2002/2005, Tommy Ramone was the only original member of the Ramones still alive, following the deaths of Joey, Johnny, and Dee Dee. "And only one of the original Ramones is still left alive. Joey, Johnny and DD are all gone. All we have left is Tommy."

xref.title: Contribution to the Formation of The Ramones
xref.body: Henry Goldrich indirectly played a role in the formation of The Ramones. In 1973, Douglas Colvin and John Cummings visited Manie's Music after deciding to form a band while high. They purchased a guitar, a bass, and a small amp from the store, which were the foundational instruments for the band they would form a year later, as D.D. and Johnny Ramone with Joey and Tommy Ramone. "The Ramones, another band made possible by Henry Goldrich, the proprietor of Manie's music in New York."

xref.title: Early Career - Tommy Ramone's Connection
xref.body: Tommy (Ramone), who later became the drummer for The Ramones, was a recording engineer who had previously worked with Jimi Hendrix. "And their manager, Tommy, a recording engineer who once worked with Jimmy Hendrix, took over on drums."

xref.title: Original Lineup and Roles
xref.body: The initial lineup included Jeff Hyman (Joey Ramone) on drums, a "6'6-inch skinny guy" and "OCD-suffering refugee from a failed band called Sniper." Their first gig was in March. By July, Jeff Hyman moved to lead vocals because he was a better singer than drummer, and their manager, Tommy (Tommy Ramone), a recording engineer who had worked with Jimi Hendrix, took over on drums. "Their drummer was a 6'6-inch skinny guy named Jeff Heimann, an OCD-suffering refugee from a failed band called Sniper."

xref.title: Ramones' Cancer Cluster Theory
xref.body: The cancers suffered by D.D., Johnny, and Tommy Ramone, as well as their art director Arturo Vega, are suspected by some to be a result of toxic residue from chemicals used in a former plastic flower factory. The factory was located in a loft on East Second Street where the Ramones rehearsed and printed t-shirts, with these chemicals believed to have permeated the entire building. "Some suspect these cancers are the result of the conditions of a loft on East Second Street, where the Ramones were heurst and printed t-shirts."

xref.title: Tommy Ramone's Death and Illness
xref.body: Tommy Ramone died in Queens, New York, on July 11, 2014, at the age of 65, after spending some time in hospice care due to bile duct cancer. "Tommy died in Queens, New York on July 11, 2014 at the age of 65."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tommy Ramone's Death and Later Career
xref.body: After leaving the Ramones, Tommy Ramone co-produced two more of their albums (*Road to Ruin* and *Too Tough to Die*) and produced albums for bands like The Replacements and Red Cross, before forming the bluegrass folk band Uncle Monk. He was diagnosed with bile duct cancer, which spread throughout his body despite treatment, and he died in hospice care on July 11, 2014, at the age of 65. "Tommy was diagnosed with bile duct cancer and spread throughout his body despite treatment. And he died at hospice care on July 11, 2014 at the age of 65."

xref.title: Tommy Ramone's Departure
xref.body: Tommy Ramone played his final show with the band on New Year's Eve 1977. He decided to leave his position as drummer to focus on his career in the recording studio, frustrated by the band's lack of commercial success, zero radio airplay, and constant touring demands. He also grew depressed with "idiot fans" and issues with Johnny's strict discipline. "Tommy got very depressed at the situation. And at some of the idiot fans that were starting to dominate gigs, there were issues with Johnny and his hardcore discipline style, something that Tommy didn't really appreciate."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tommy Ramone's Departure and Replacement
xref.body: Tommy Ramone remained with the band until 1978, at which point he was replaced by Marky Ramone. "He stayed with the band until 1978, when he was replaced by Marki Ramon."

xref.title: Tommy Ramone's Early Career and Production Role
xref.body: Tommy Erdelyi (Tommy Ramone) escaped communism as a child, fleeing Hungary with his parents to New York. He was a skilled guitarist and, significantly, worked as a recording engineer at The Record Plant, where he notably worked with Jimi Hendrix. This experience led him to produce the Ramones' first three albums, and later co-produced their fourth and eighth albums. "Not only did he play guitar, but he also found a very sweet gig working as a recording engineer in a studio called the Record Plant. One of the very first people he got to work for was Jimmy Hendricks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tommy Ramone's Family Background
xref.body: Tommy Ramone, whose real name was Tamis Urdelje, was the Jewish son of a Holocaust survivor from Hungary. "His real name was Tamis Urdelje, the Jewish son of a Holocaust survivor from Hungary."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tommy Ramone's Initial Role and Transition to Drummer
xref.body: The first iteration of the Ramones featured D.D. on vocals and bass, Johnny on guitar, and Joey on drums, with Tommy initially intended to be their manager. However, when Joey transitioned to vocals, Tommy was recruited into the band as the drummer. "Tommy was supposed to be their manager, but when Joey moved to vocals, Tommy was drafted into the position."
